newsitem.title: USA: Carnival seen protecting earnings in deal.
newsitem.headline: Carnival seen protecting earnings in deal.

text.p: Carnival Corp has offered a rich price to wrest Celebrity Cruise Lines Inc from rival Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd, but the Miami-based firm is not expected to jeopardize earnings performance for a deal.
Known for financial conservatism, Carnival would likely abandon the effort if it threatened to dilute earnings, said Wall Street analysts who spoke with company officials.
"If it works, and it works out to be non-dilutive, it's terrific. If it looks to be dilutive, presumably Carnival will not pursue it," said Joseph Buckley of Bear Stearns & Co Inc.

Carnival late Wednesday said it offered to buy Celebrity for $525 million, topping a $500 million deal struck nine days ago with Royal Caribbean. In a statement announcing the offer, Carnival said it did not think the deal would dilute earnings.
The Carnival offer calls for cash or a mixture of cash and stock, while the Royal Caribbean transaction is a cash and stock deal.
A spokesman for Carnival did not comment specifically on whether the company would walk away from a dilutive transaction, saying only "it has been our policy not to do dilutive deals".
Because Celebrity is privately owned, Carnival has limited access to information on the company's financial performance.

Celebrity is jointly owned by Overseas Shipholding Group Inc and privately held Chandris Group. In its letter offering $525 million, Carnival said it may be willing to increase the bid if it gained access to Celebrity's financial documents.

Overseas Shipholding confirmed it had received the Carnival offer, saying it would contact Carnival if it was interested. Carnival also disclosed it had offered to buy Celebrity for $510 million in cash three days ago.

Royal Caribbean could not be reached for comment. Company executives met with Wall Street analysts on Thursday for a previously scheduled conference, but declined to discuss the competing offer, said analysts who attended the meeting.
Analysts said Carnival would likely have little problem integrating Celebrity into its portfolio. Carnival recently completed the acquisition of Italian cruise company Costa Crociere SpA.
"Carnival has done a lot of acquisitions in its day and integrated many brands. If anyone can maximize Celebrity's potential, Carnival can," Jill Krutick of Smith Barney said.

They also said Carnival would gain a valuable presence in the Bermuda market with an acquisition of Celebrity. which holds a 40 percent market share there. Carnival does not have a presence in Bermuda.
